prompt:
Write 10 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1401; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened for a left-turn collision at an intersection with a reported whiplash injury. The insured's driver is listed on the policy, and the claimant is represented by counsel, so all contact will be routed through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Police report and two statements confirm the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of impact. No independent witnesses have come forward to describe how the collision happened.

Entry 3: Photos from the scene and the repair shop show damage consistent with the impact described by both drivers. Nothing in the file points to earlier damage on the vehicle, and nothing suggests the damage predates the policy's coverage start.

Entry 4: Recorded call with the claimant's attorney. The client's account of the turn and the impact matches what was told at first notice, with no changes in the details.

Entry 5: Medical records received for the initial emergency visit. The diagnosis of whiplash is plausible for a rear-quarter impact at this speed, and no earlier treatment to the neck or upper back appears in the records.

Entry 6: Reviewed the prior claims history and the claimant's medical history with the claimant's consent. No earlier injury to the same body area is on file.

Entry 7: Physical therapy notes received. Treatment followed a usual course for this type of injury, with visits tapering off as the claimant's range of motion improved.

Entry 8: Spoke again with the claimant's attorney to confirm the remaining treatment schedule. The claimant has been consistent about symptoms and history in every conversation so far.

Entry 9: Reviewed the repair estimate against the photos and the impact description. The damage pattern matches the reported collision, and the repair scope is in line with the vehicle's make and model.

Entry 10: Final review completed. The reported injury, treatment course, and vehicle damage all line up with the described loss, and the file is ready for settlement evaluation.
